newsitem.title: CANADA: Parti Quebecois/Liberals split Quebec by-elections.
newsitem.headline: Parti Quebecois/Liberals split Quebec by-elections.

text.p: The separatist Parti Quebecois government and the opposition Liberals each won one of two special elections held in Quebec on Monday.
The Parti Quebecois won the Prevost riding by 233 votes over the Liberals. Prevost had been held by a Parti Quebecois cabinet minister who resigned.
The Liberals swept the Beauce-Sud riding by 15,481 votes over the Parti Quebecois. The francophone riding has never elected a Parti Quebecois candidate and has been staunchly federalist.
In both special elections, the Liberals improved on their results from the 1994 Quebec general election. In 1994, the Liberals won Beauce-Sud by only 159 votes and lost Prevost by 4,253 votes.
In Quebec's National Assembly, the Parti Quebecois has 74 seats, versus 46 for the Liberals and one for the Action Democratique. Two seats are held by independents and two are vacant.
